name: DPRK IT-worker applications to defense-related organizations

attribution.legal_posture: Source-attributed aggregate or sector-targeting telemetry; affected-organization finding, adjudication, successful employment, and compromise remain unreported.

caveats: Applications are application-stage records; successful hiring, access, compromise, data theft and a named affected organization require separate evidence.
Adjacent DPRK espionage or fake-recruiter malware activity stays outside the IT-worker record unless an explicit source link connects it.

statements: GTIG observed evidence of DPRK IT workers applying to jobs at defense-related organizations.
GTIG frames personnel and hiring processes as a defense-sector attack surface that can evade conventional enterprise-security visibility.
limitations: Applications do not establish successful hiring, access, compromise, data theft, or a named affected organization.
Do not merge adjacent DPRK espionage or fake-recruiter malware activity into the IT-worker record without explicit source bridging.

sources.support: GTIG states that personnel and hiring processes are part of the defense-sector attack surface and that it observed evidence of DPRK IT workers applying to jobs at defense-related organizations. It describes the activity as continuing through 2025 and incorporating publicly available tooling. Evidence boundary: Sector-targeting telemetry. Evidence of applications is not evidence of successful employment, access, compromise, theft, or a named affected organization. Adjacent malware and espionage sections are separate activity unless explicitly bridged
sources.locator: Section 2, “Employees in the Crosshairs”; subsection “North Korea’s Insider Threat and Revenue Generation”
